state.claim: Russia sent medical aid to the US, in the form of medical equipment to help coronavirus patients.

records.title: Russia Sends Emergency Medical Aid to United States
records.retrieval_query: Did Russia send medical equipment to the United States intended to help coronavirus patients, and on what date(s) did any such shipment occur?

passages.P1: # Russia Sends Emergency Medical Aid to United States
passages.P4: Russian President Vladimir Putin chairs a Security Council meeting at the Novo-Ogaryovo residence outside Moscow Moscow, Russia, Friday, Feb. 21, 2020. (Alexei Druzhinin, Sputnik, Kremlin Pool Photo via AP)
passages.P5: MOSCOW — Russia has sent a planeload of medical aid to the United States amid the growing coronavirus pandemic.
passages.P6: A military aircraft loaded with medical equipment and masks took off from Moscow early Wednesday morning, according to the Defense Ministry.
passages.P7: Footage from the Russian Defense Ministry showed boxes of equipment inside an Antonov An-124 Ruslan aircraft at Moscow’s Chkalovsky Airbase.
passages.P8: Russian President Vladimir Putin chairs a Security Council meeting at the Novo-Ogaryovo residence outside Moscow Moscow, Russia, Friday, Feb. 21, 2020. (Alexei Druzhinin, Sputnik, Kremlin Pool Photo via AP)
passages.P9: The delivery follows a phone call between President Vladimir Putin and President Trump on Monday, when they discussed cooperation in the fight against the new coronavirus. A Kremlin statement said the call took place at Washington’s initiative.
passages.P10: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Tuesday that Trump accepted Russia’s aid “with gratitude.”
passages.P11: “Offering aid to the American colleagues, the president (Vladimir Putin) is assuming that when American production of medical equipment and materials picks up speed, they will be able to reciprocate if necessary,” Peskov told the Interfax news agency.
passages.P13: LONDON (AP) — The British government is under fire for failing to keep its promise to increase the number of tests performed for Covid-19.
passages.P14: The U.K. has restricted testing to hospitalized patients, leaving many people with milder symptoms unsure whether they have had the new coronavirus. Many scientists have urged wider testing to allow medics who are negative to remain at work, and to better understand how the virus spreads.
passages.P15: That has happened in Germany, which has the capacity to do 500,000 tests a week.
passages.P16: The U.K. initially performed about 5,000 tests a day, but the government promised to increase that number to 10,000 by the end of last week. The target has not been met, with just over 8,000 tests performed Monday, the last day for which figures were available.
passages.P17: Officials blamed a shortage of the chemicals needed to perform the tests.
passages.P18: Communities secretary Robert Jenrick said Wednesday that the number of tests should hit 15,000 a day “within a couple of days” and rise to 25,000 a day by mid-April. He conceded, “We do need to go further and we need to do that faster.”
passages.P19: He told ITV that “it isn’t easy to procure the tests in a global pandemic because there is a great deal of demand.”
passages.P21: LONDON — Britain’s largest banks are scrapping dividend payments amid pressure to secure cash for businesses struggling with the fallout of the Covid-19 pandemic.
passages.P22: The Bank of England’s Prudential Regulation Authority requested the suspension of all plans to return money to shareholders. All outstanding dividend payments from last year will also be canceled.
passages.P23: Barclays, Lloyds and NatWest are among the banks accepting the move.
passages.P24: The PRA says the decisions “are a sensible precautionary step given the unique role that banks need to play in supporting the wider economy through a period of economic disruption, alongside the extraordinary measures being taken by the authorities.''
passages.P25: The authority also expects bonuses to be canceled for senior staff members.

records.title: Russian plane with coronavirus medical gear lands in U.S. after ...
records.retrieval_query: Did Russia send medical equipment to the United States intended to help coronavirus patients, and on what date(s) did any such shipment occur?

passages.P1: MOSCOW/WASHINGTON - Russia sent the United States medical equipment on Wednesday to help fight the coronavirus pandemic, a public relations coup for Russian President Vladimir Putin after he discussed the crisis with U.S. President Donald Trump.
passages.P2: Trump, struggling to fill shortages of ventilators and personal protective equipment, accepted Putin's offer in a phone call on Monday. A Russian military transport plane left an airfield outside Moscow and arrived at New York's John F. Kennedy airport in late afternoon on Wednesday.
passages.P3: Emergency aid to Washington was a striking development. Usually, the United States donates supplies to embattled countries rather than accepting them. The origin of the gift was bound to revive criticism from Democrats that Trump has been too cozy with the Russian leader.
passages.P4: "Trump gratefully accepted this humanitarian aid," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov was cited as saying by the Interfax news agency on Tuesday. Trump himself spoke enthusiastically about the Russian help after his call with Putin.
passages.P5: A U.S. official in Washington confirmed the shipment was a direct result of Trump's phone conversation with Putin. The official said it carried 60 tons of ventilators, masks, respirators and other items.
passages.P6: The official said the equipment would be carefully examined to make sure it comports with the quality requirements of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
passages.P7: Russia's Rossiya 24 channel on Wednesday morning showed the plane taking off from a military air base outside Moscow in darkness. Its cargo hold was filled with cardboard boxes and other packages.
passages.P8: ### FOR SUBSCRIBERSVoters want the Iran war to end. It’s not that easy.
passages.P9: ### FOR SUBSCRIBERSAre we approaching a new era of Alzheimer’s prevention?
passages.P10: Confirmed U.S. coronavirus cases have surged to more than 205,000, with 4,500 deaths.
passages.P11: In Russia, the official tally of confirmed cases is 2,337, with 17 deaths, although some doctors there have questioned the accuracy of official data.
passages.P13: ### FOR SUBSCRIBERSVoters want the Iran war to end. It’s not that easy.
passages.P14: ### FOR SUBSCRIBERSAre we approaching a new era of Alzheimer’s prevention?
passages.P15: Relations between Moscow and Washington have been strained in recent years by everything from Syria to Ukraine to U.S. election interference, something Russia denies. Trump spent two years battling a federal investigation into whether his 2016 campaign colluded with Russia.
passages.P16: "Nothing to see here. Just a Russian military aircraft landing at JFK with 60 tons of medical supplies to support America’s #COVID19 response. A propaganda bonanza as our own government shrinks from America’s leadership role in a global crisis," said Brett McGurk, a former American diplomat for Trump and former Presidents Barack Obama and George W. Bush.
passages.P17: Trump said on Tuesday he and Putin discussed the virus at length. "Russia is being hit pretty hard," he said.
passages.P18: Peskov, Putin's spokesman, said Moscow hoped the United States might also be able to provide medical help to Russia if necessary when the time came.
passages.P19: "It is important to note that when offering assistance to U.S. colleagues, the president (Putin) assumes that when U.S. manufacturers of medical equipment and materials gain momentum, they will also be able to reciprocate if necessary," Peskov was cited as saying.

records.title: Russia bills US $660K for aid that included gas masks ...
records.retrieval_query: What specific medical equipment was reportedly included in any Russian aid shipment to the US, and how was it described by Russian and US officials?

passages.P5: # Russia bills US $660K for aid that included gas masks, household cleaning gloves
passages.P6: Details of cargo raise question about how much of the shipment was useful.
passages.P8: Russia billed the U.S. nearly $660,000 for its medical aid flight last month that included thousands of pieces of equipment not typically used by hospitals, including chemical warfare-style gas masks and household cleaning gloves, according to a government record of the shipment.
passages.P9: The cargo also included 45 ventilators that were not immediately useable because of voltage-related issues, according to two U.S. officials.
passages.P10: It was not immediately clear how useful the April 1 shipment to New York City’s John F. Kennedy airport has been for nearby hospitals. The federal government said it transferred the supplies to New York and New Jersey state officials, who did not immediately respond to questions about whether the cargo was provided to health care workers or remains in storage.
passages.P11: Thousands of respirators, surgical gloves, medical clothing and antiseptic packets were also included in the flight.
passages.P12: Still, the details and price tag of the shipment, which have not been previously reported, challenge public descriptions by the Kremlin and President Donald Trump and raise questions about whether the shipment served primarily as a public relations coup for Russia, known by U.S. intelligence for waging disinformation campaigns.
passages.P13: “I’m not concerned about Russian propaganda. Not even a little bit,” Trump told reporters during an April 2 press briefing.
passages.P14: Russian President Vladimir Putin chairs a video conference meeting with heads of Russia's regions over the COVID-19, coronavirus pandemic at the Novo-Ogaryovo state residence outside Moscow on April 28, 2020.
passages.P16: Trump said the cargo was offered by Russian President Vladimir Putin in a private phone call.
passages.P17: “He offered a lot of medical, high quality stuff that I accepted and that may save a lot of lives. I’ll take it every day,” Trump said.
passages.P18: Moscow referred to the flight in its state-run media as “humanitarian aid” that New Yorkers would be grateful to receive. Russia’s foreign ministry said the Kremlin was covering the cost of half the value of the cargo with the other half being covered by the United States.
passages.P19: “In New York, there really is a tough situation, it seems to me, every make, every piece of protective gear counts, and so it’s hard to overstate the importance of this aid,” said Dmitry Polyansky told Russian reporters after meeting the plane at JFK airport, according to the state news agency TASS.
passages.P20: “It’s a good gesture of solidarity with New Yorkers. They appreciate it,” he said.
passages.P22: “It was a very nice gesture on behalf of President Putin and I could have said ‘no thank you’ or I could have said ‘thank you’ and it was a large plane of very high-quality medical supplies, and I said ‘I’ll take it,’” Trump told reporters April 2.
passages.P23: Foreign policy experts though have questioned the move by Trump, saying it was a propaganda coup for the Kremlin as it continues to try to undercut U.S. interests.
passages.P24: A Russian military transport plane carrying medical equipment, masks and supplies lands at JFK International Airport during the outbreak of the coronavirus disease in New York, April 1, 2020.

records.title: A Mystery Wrapped In An Enigma Inside A Russian Coronavirus ...
records.retrieval_query: What specific medical equipment was reportedly included in any Russian aid shipment to the US, and how was it described by Russian and US officials?

passages.P1: # A Mystery Wrapped In An Enigma Inside A Russian Coronavirus Aid Shipment To The U.S.
passages.P4: It was a coronavirus aid shipment that already had raised eyebrows in both the United States and Russia.
passages.P5: A Russian Defense Ministry cargo jet loaded with masks, ventilators, and other medical equipment arrived at New York's John F. Kennedy International Airport on April 1: It was "humanitarian assistance," according to the Kremlin, to help the United States in its fight against COVID-19.
passages.P6: Later that same day, however, the State Department contradicted the Kremlin: No, in fact, the United States had purchased the shipment from Russia. The State Department declined to say how much was paid.
passages.P7: A day later, Russia's Foreign Ministry spoke up, saying that Moscow and Washington had split the cost.
passages.P8: Now there's another wrinkle: two of the Russian entities involved in the shipment were hit with sanctions by the U.S. administration as part of Western punishment imposed for the seizure of Ukraine's Crimean Peninsula in 2014.
passages.P9: Adding yet further confusion: An anonymous U.S. administration official was quoted as saying that contrary to the Russian statement, the cost was not shared -- the United States paid for the entire shipment.
passages.P10: The back-and-forth raised questions among observers: Did the United States violate its own sanctions, or carve out a special exemption to allow the shipment to go forward? If so, why? And why the conflicting accounts about the payment?
passages.P12: Days earlier, U.S. President Donald Trump made passing reference to the aid shipment, saying it came up during a phone call he had with his Russian counterpart, Vladimir Putin. But he spoke about it as if it had already occurred.
passages.P13: On April 2, Trump was asked by reporters about the shipment, and specifically whether he thought it could be used as a part of a propaganda message by the Kremlin.
passages.P14: "He was very nice," Trump said of his phone call with Putin. "He said: 'We have it…. They have difficulties with this virus also, as you know. It was a very nice gesture on behalf of President Putin. I could have said 'No.' But I said: 'I'll take it.'"
passages.P15: "I'm not concerned about Russia and propaganda, not even a little bit. There is a lot of medical, very high-quality stuff that I've accepted. It may save a lot of lives and I will take it every day," he said.
passages.P16: Western and Russian critics of Moscow say that the Kremlin is using aid as part of a propaganda campaign amid the global coronavirus pandemic.
passages.P17: In Moscow, Russian state media broadcast stories about the shipment, including footage of the Antonov cargo jet being loaded with supplies. The cardboard boxes were printed with the words "From Russia With Love."
passages.P18: Russia's ambassador to the United States said in a post to the embassy's official Facebook page that he hoped the U.S. government would help Russia in the future, if needed -- "without any politicization."
passages.P19: "We can provide emergency equipment needed to save Americans. The Russian humanitarian mission can already be successful even if a single life is saved," Anatoly Antonov said. "We are sure that the U.S., if necessary, will also assist us and we will gladly accept the aid. Without any politicization."
passages.P21: In his second major televised address on the coronavirus crisis in Russia, shown the day the jet arrived in New York, on April 2, Putin did not mention the shipment.
